title: Graph-Augmented Dense Retrieval for Wikipedia Wikilink Target Prediction
one_liner: Train and evaluate a production-grade Transformer bi-encoder augmented with Wikipedia’s link graph to retrieve the correct target page from hyperlink context at million-scale.
research_question: Under a strict page-level holdout split, how much does incorporating Wikipedia link-graph structure (via learned node embeddings + neighbor aggregation) improve wikilink target retrieval versus strong sparse (BM25/TF-IDF) and text-only dense baselines?

dataset.name: Wikimedia Dumps: English Wikipedia pages-articles + pagelinks
dataset.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikipedia content; dumps distributed under the same content license terms)
dataset.ingestion_notes: Pipeline downloads dumps directly (no credentials), streams decompression/parsing, extracts (1) per-page text (title + lead paragraphs) and (2) wikilinks with local context windows around anchors. Build a deterministic documented subset: keep top N target pages by in-link frequency (e.g., N=200k) and sample M link instances (e.g., M=3M train / 200k val / 200k test) with a page-level split (hold out entire source pages to prevent leakage). Expect large temporary disk usage (often 80–150GB) during extraction unless configured to early-stop at N pages / M links.

method.model: Dual-encoder retrieval with PyTorch: Query encoder = Transformer over anchor-context (e.g., 128–256 tokens); Doc encoder = Transformer over target page title+lead. Learn with in-batch contrastive loss (InfoNCE) over (context, target_page) pairs. Add graph augmentation: learn page node embeddings from the pagelinks graph using a GraphSAGE-style neighbor-mean aggregator (implemented in pure PyTorch with sampled neighbors) and fuse with doc text embedding via a learned gated residual (doc = text + gate(context,text,graph)*graph). Optional second-stage cross-encoder reranker for top-100 candidates to improve Recall@K and MRR.
method.baseline: Sparse retrieval baseline: TF-IDF (or BM25-style scoring) over target page title+lead; query is anchor-context. Evaluate as a pure lexical retriever on the same candidate set and splits.
ablations: Text-only dense retriever (disable graph embeddings and fusion).
Graph-only target representations (use only learned node embeddings for docs; keep query encoder text-based).
No gating fusion (simple concat + MLP vs gated residual) to isolate fusion mechanism effect.
Context window size ablation (64 vs 256 tokens) to quantify how much local context drives disambiguation.
Reranker ablation (bi-encoder only vs bi-encoder + cross-encoder rerank) to isolate second-stage gains.
metrics: Recall@1/10/100 on held-out wikilinks (retrieval over candidate target pages).
Calibration diagnostics for top-1 confidence (ECE on softmax over candidate set sampled negatives).
Throughput and cost metrics (docs/sec, queries/sec, GPU memory, index build time).

risks: Download time and disk pressure: dumps are large; extraction can temporarily balloon disk usage depending on settings.
Parsing complexity: Wikipedia markup and redirects/disambiguation can introduce noisy targets; requires robust filtering (redirect resolution, namespace filtering, minimum-text thresholds).

Evaluation leakage if splits are not page-level: link contexts from the same source page can be near-duplicates; must hold out entire source pages and optionally entire target pages for a tougher setting.
Graph scale: full pagelinks is huge; must subset to top-linked pages and neighbor-sample to keep training tractable on a single machine.
Bias/coverage: frequent entities dominate; needs stratified reporting by target popularity buckets to avoid misleading average improvements.
execution_steps: Create environment: `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -U pip`.

Install deps: `pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121 && pip install transformers datasets accelerate sentencepiece scikit-learn numpy pandas pyarrow faiss-gpu tqdm`.
Download dumps: `python scripts/download_wiki.py --out data/raw --latest` (fetch pages-articles + pagelinks from Wikimedia URLs).

Extract corpus + link contexts: `python scripts/extract_wikilinks.py --pages_xml data/raw/enwiki-latest-pages-articles.xml.bz2 --pagelinks_sql data/raw/enwiki-latest-pagelinks.sql.gz --out data/processed --top_targets 200000 --train_links 3000000 --val_links 200000 --test_links 200000 --split page_holdout`.

Build sparse baseline index: `python scripts/build_tfidf_index.py --corpus data/processed/target_pages.parquet --out data/index/tfidf` and evaluate: `python scripts/eval_sparse.py --queries data/processed/test_links.parquet --index data/index/tfidf --k 100`.

Train text-only bi-encoder: `accelerate launch train_biencoder.py --train data/processed/train_links.parquet --corpus data/processed/target_pages.parquet --model distilroberta-base --fp16 --batch_size 128 --gpus 2 --out runs/text_only`.
Train graph embeddings: `python train_graphsage.py --edges data/processed/pagelinks_edges.parquet --nodes data/processed/target_pages.parquet --neighbors 10 --layers 2 --dim 256 --out runs/graph`.

Train fused model (text+graph): `accelerate launch train_fused.py --train data/processed/train_links.parquet --corpus data/processed/target_pages.parquet --text_ckpt runs/text_only --graph_ckpt runs/graph --fusion gated_residual --out runs/text_graph`.

Evaluate dense retrievers: `python eval_dense.py --queries data/processed/test_links.parquet --corpus data/processed/target_pages.parquet --ckpt runs/text_only --k 100` and `python eval_dense.py --ckpt runs/text_graph --k 100`.
Run ablations (toggle flags in the same training/eval scripts) and produce a single table + plots: `python scripts/report.py --runs runs/ --out reports/wikilink_retrieval.html`.
